title: Flux decline during cross-flow ultrafiltration of whey protein concentrate: effect of pH and ionic strength on cake layer resistance

record.title: Flux decline during cross-flow ultrafiltration of whey protein concentrate: effect of pH and ionic strength on cake layer resistance
record.abstract: Flux decline was examined during dead-end and cross-flow ultrafiltration of whey protein concentrate (WPC-35) using 10 kDa polyethersulphone membranes at pH values of 4.6, 6.0, and 7.0 and NaCl concentrations of 0, 50, and 150 mM. Flux was measured at transmembrane pressures of 1–4 bar at 25 °C. The cake filtration and intermediate blocking models were fitted to experimental flux–volume data. At pH 4.6 (near the isoelectric point of β-lactoglobulin), specific cake resistance increased by a factor of 3.2 compared with pH 7.0, attributed to denser packing of aggregated protein particles. Ionic strength of 150 mM reduced electrostatic repulsion and increased resistance by 40% relative to salt-free conditions. Scanning electron microscopy of the membrane surface confirmed a compact, heterogeneous deposit at low pH. The results provide quantitative input for process design when handling acid whey fractions.
